candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record demonstrates rate-dependent LBBB appearing at HR 107 bpm with chest pain and resolving on cessation — the hallmark of Painful LBBB Syndrome (Chatterjee phenomenon). Cardiac Syndrome X shares the features of exertional chest pain and normal coronary angiography/CTA but is a distinct entity defined by microvascular dysfunction without the obligatory LBBB finding. Labeling this as Cardiac Syndrome X omits the critical LBBB component and asserts a different mechanistic subtype.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Cardiac Syndrome X is microvascular angina with normal epicardial coronaries but does not specifically involve rate-dependent LBBB; the benchmark requires the LBBB component as the defining diagnostic entity

case_quality_flags: Classic presentation of rate-dependent Painful LBBB Syndrome with clear ECG documentation; coronary CTA normal, no ischemic T-wave changes — well-supported benchmark diagnosis
